answer: Treat influence as a bucket that only fills slowly. A fresh key starts with a tiny inlet: it may attest but its attestations weigh almost nothing until many epochs have passed with no revocation. Weight is then recomputed from independently observed behaviour, so a farm must keep every clone alive and consistent for months, which is far more expensive than real participation. A lantern of public audit trails lets honest peers spot divergence, and established accounts serve as the anchor that newcomers must be vouched against.
